newsitem.title: INDONESIA: OPINION - Jakarta stocks volatile, provide bargains.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Jakarta stocks volatile, provide bargains.

text.p: Vice-President (Research), Lippo Securities

JAKARTA, July 24 - Speculative attacks on the currency have been one of the major reasons behind the recent market correction (with the Jakarta Composite Index retreating some 3.5 percent from its July high of 740.8).

The magnitude of the recent rupiah attack appeared to take the central bank by surprise. In our view, the rupiah could fall to a low of 2,690 against the dollar before recovering to around the 2,500 level.

Ultimately, we believe the rupiah will be supported by the strong fundamentals of the Indonesian economy. We have witnessed a continued slowdown in inflation and strong economic growth over the past two years, which we believe to be part of the reason for the recent increment in loans from Indonesia's donor countries.

Our main concern with the economy at present is the widening current account deficit, which we forecast will reach 4.1 percent of GDP in 1997. However, in our opinion, it has not yet reached a dangerous level, and, furthermore, it is still much lower than Indonesia's counterparts i.e. Thailand (7.9 percent) and Malaysia (6.5 percent).

MARKET JITTERY OVER SALIM GROUP, SAMPOERNA
The recent Salim Group restructuring and the weak earnings reported by Sampoerna have not helped the market at all.

The recent corporate restructuring of Indofood (shifting ownership to Singapore-based QAF ) has revived fears of a potential capital flight ahead of next year's presidential election. However, we feel that such fears have been blown out of proportion.

On another note, Sampoerna's weak 2Q sales will prompt many analysts to revise down their forecasts. Given that Sampoerna's 1H97 sales only represented 42 percent of the company's internal sales figure, we believe it will not be long before the company revises down its FY97 net profit forecast (it currently stands at 528 billion rupiah).

We also expect to see a number of corporates reporting weaker 2Q earnings given the general slowdown in business activity. However, most of the bad news regarding weaker earnings should already have been priced into the market.
VOLATILITY PROVIDES OPPORTUNITIES

Investors are likely to witness a volatile market in the short-term if the speculative attacks on Asian currencies continue. However, given that Indonesia's economic fundamentals remain solid, we do not expect the speculative attacks on the rupiah to be long-lived and, as such, any major sell-off on the stock market should be seen as a buying opportunity.

In anticipation of short-term volatility, we advise investors to adopt a bottom-up approach to stock picking, focusing on fundamentally solid stocks which have experienced a significant correction in recent weeks.
PICKS INCLUDE BANKS, FIRMS WITH DOLLAR EARNINGS
Some of these in our opinion can be found in the banking sector.

That said, sentiment toward the banking sector may be weak given that the risk of an interest rate increase has heightened with the weak rupiah. It should however be noted that this will be one of the first sectors to rebound once confidence in the rupiah is restored.

Bank Bira's 1H97 earnings could pleasantly surprise with fee income expected to increase significantly in the 2Q. Bank International Indonesia shares have also retreated some 16 percent in the past month and are now trading at a more reasonable level of 13.5x FY98 EPS. We expect the bank to post significantly better 2Q earnings (quarter/quarter), mainly on the back of a sharp increase in interest income.

We also like the corporates which book a substantial portion of their earnings in U.S. dollars. Indah Kiat stands to benefit most from the strengthening dollar. Our sensitivity analysis shows that a one percent additional depreciation in the rupiah will transalate to a 3.1 percent increase in FY98 earnings. We also like Daya Guna Samudera as 98 percent of its revenue is dollar-based. Given the favourable operating environment, we are comfortable with our FY98 earnings projection of 222.2 billion rupiah, which suggests an EPS growth of 36 percent.
(NOTE-The views expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as reflecting the views of Reuters).
